summary: IntrepidOne bridges macro NASA Earth observations with street-level pedestrian navigation to mitigate Urban Heat Island (UHI) risks in historic cities like Rome. While commercial navigation apps optimize solely for distance, IntrepidOne acts as a dual-core climate resilience engine: (1) an Earth System Trend Detective powered by 30 years of NASA POWER (MERRA-2) reanalysis data (1995–2024), utilizing Mann-Kendall and Sen's Slope non-parametric statistics to prove statistically significant warming trends (p < 0.05); and (2) a microclimate pedestrian router that models building shadows (H/W aspect ratios) and urban tree canopy coverage to route citizens along cool, shaded corridors (reducing radiative thermal exposure by up to -8.9 °C). Deployed live on Streamlit Cloud with an open-source architecture, IntrepidOne protects vulnerable commuters and equips municipal planners with downloadable climate anomaly datasets.
details:
The Challenge and Motivation Urban Heat Islands (UHI) turn summer commutes in dense historic cities like Rome into acute health risks. Traditional weather forecasts provide city-wide averages, leaving pedestrians blind to block-by-block temperature spikes on unshaded asphalt.

How It Works (Dual-Core Architecture) IntrepidOne integrates macro climate science with local urban physics through an interactive web platform (intrepidone.streamlit.app):

  1. Macro Climate Trend Detective (Tab 1): Ingests 30-year (1995-2024) daily records from the NASA POWER API (MERRA-2 assimilation model), tracking Air Temperature (T2M), Daily Max (T2M_MAX), Skin Temperature (TS), and Solar Insolation. It applies the Mann-Kendall test and Theil-Sen's Slope estimator to quantify exact decadal warming rates and verify statistical significance (p < 0.05).
  2. Cool-Shade Micro-Routing (Tab 2): Implements a parametric urban microclimate simulation for Rome, combining building canyon geometry (H/W) and tree canopy evapotranspiration (e.g., Pinus pinea) to compute shade-optimized pedestrian pathways versus exposed direct routes.
  3. Civic and Municipal Data Export (Tab 3): Provides transparent methodology documentation alongside a one-click CSV export of processed 30-year NASA climate anomalies for urban planners.

Expected Impact

  • For Citizens: Direct protection from extreme heat stress and heatstroke during peak hours for commuters, tourists, and vulnerable populations.
  • For Urban Planners: Empirical evidence and downloadable datasets to prioritize green infrastructure and targeted tree-canopy investments.

Technology Stack

  • Backend and Statistics: Python, pymannkendall, scipy.stats, pandas, numpy.
  • Frontend and Mapping: Streamlit, Plotly.js, Folium and Leaflet.js heatmaps.
